verdict.rationale: Gmail's own filters are rules that evaluate incoming mail and automatically add or remove labels or forward messages without user intervention. That counts as genuine background automation, and a community user confirms routing mail with a filter. The scope is narrow, though: rule-triggered label and forward actions only, with no evidenced AI-driven or agentic background automation. Gemini actions are on-demand, and push notifications and the API are developer building blocks that earn no credit. missing for 10: autonomous AI/agent-driven automations, recurring or scheduled automation runs, richer action types beyond labeling/forwarding, in-depth independent corroboration of autonomous background operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: When a message matches, filters automatically trigger actions such as adding or removing labels, or forwarding the email to a specified address.
Advanced rules configured for an account that evaluate incoming messages against specific matching criteria (like sender, subject, or size).
After you search, you can use the results to set up a filter for these messages.
